svg.title: Archimedes’ principle
svg.desc: (a) An object submerged in a fluid has weight w_obj acting down and a buoyant force F_B acting up; in this case the weight is larger, so the object sinks. (b) If the object is removed, the space it occupied fills with fluid of weight w_fl. That fluid is held up by the same buoyant force, so F_B = w_fl: the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced. A free-body diagram beside each panel shows the forces. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Buoyant force equals the displaced fluid’s weight
The object is lowered externally. Buoyancy increases during entry, then stays constant when fully
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
